decisions.reason: As a flagship service that directly extends the firm’s core cloud messaging capabilities, it fits existing knowledge deeply and is well positioned to be refined through the firm’s own R&D.

Document capture and recognition is somewhat broader than pure messaging but still complements electronic document workflows, so the firm’s related expertise and development capacity make continuation more likely than withdrawal.

Email and fax conversion builds on the firm’s established multichannel communications base and should remain useful for customers bridging legacy and digital processes, despite only modest initial prominence.
This optimization feature is close to the existing fax business and easy for the firm to absorb and improve, though its narrower scope makes it a bit more disposable than the main service launches.
Threat protection strongly matches the firm’s secure messaging position, and with in-house R&D the firm has the absorptive capacity to learn from early use and enhance the service.
Multi-engine virus scanning is highly related to the firm’s security and email infrastructure capabilities, so it is likely to be retained as an incremental strengthening of the core offer.
